title: The masking rules stay in P1 in the TSD while the Ownership Map rules the table to rwb-access (P4)
source: TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.6, T3.2 and T6.3 (masking_rule created by V0001, its content owned by RWB-E1-037); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Ownership Map v1 (masking_rule, role and permission to P4); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41 (P4 owns the masking policy)
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC6; 8 Business rules BR2 and BR3; 11 Data; 12 Contract 12.7
description: The Technical Specification keeps masking_rule in P1's schema and describes P1 applying the mask itself, while the Ownership Map gives masking_rule, role and permission to rwb-access (P4) and Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 give P4 the masking policy. Read as written, the story would hold a copy of another service's table and read it by SQL, which the ownership rule, the per-service login rule and boundary rule BND-6 all forbid.
evidence: TSD P1 v3 T3.6 'masking_rule is created by V0001 and its content is owned by RWB-E1-037'; Ownership Map v1 tables.masking_rule owner P4; Architecture v5 slide 14 P4 OUT 'masking policy' and slide 41 P4 'Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy'
proposed: P1 holds data_product_access only. The masking rows, the role list and the permission matrix stay with rwb-access, and P1 takes the answer from POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise and the FieldMasker interface of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and names no masking, role or permission table in a query.

title: The data_product_access seed of the version in force is only partly specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-016 section 3 precondition on version DPA-2026.11; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.15.2 and A2.15.4 (AC-ALT-P1-015-01 and AC-ALT-P1-015-02); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 data_product_access; WP B-P1-01 story line RWB-P1-E1016-DB
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC3 and AC10; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: The sources give only part of the version that must be in force: RW-CASEOWN and RW-AUDIT read DP02, and RW-PHONECOL reads DP01, DP02, DP03 and DP05 and has no row for DP06. No source gives the rows for the other roles of the role list or for DP04 and DP07 to DP14, so the seed cannot be completed from the sources and the version is incomplete at go-live if only these rows are written.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-016 section 3 'for example RW-CASEOWN and RW-AUDIT read DP02; RW-PHONECOL reads DP01, DP02, DP03 and DP05 and not DP06'; FSD P1 v3 A2.15.4 AC-ALT-P1-015-02 with the DP06 refusal; no role-to-product matrix anywhere in the sources
proposed: Seed only the six rows the sources give under version DPA-2026.11 and leave every other role and product to a later approved load through the rwb-case reference-data contract. No row is invented, no role is granted a product by default, and the gap is closed by the data steward before the version is relied on outside SIT.

title: The monolith reference-load endpoint has no target owner for an access load
source: Legacy RWB-E1-016 section 12 'Endpoint used for the access load' (POST /admin/reference-loads and its approve path); FSD P1 v3 A2.15.2 step 1; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling (parameters and reference data to P3) and DP-07; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15
section: 4 Flow step 1; 7 Acceptance criteria AC4 and AC11; 12 Contract 12.2
description: The legacy story loads an access version through the monolith reference-load endpoint with a separate approval call and hands the approved rows to P1 through the DataProductAccessLoader interface. In the target reference data is rwb-case's (DP-07, R3 default ruling), the monolith base path is retired, and no source states the load path, the handler or the approval for this service, so the load has no agreed owner in the target.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-016 section 12 endpoint table and 'the P4 reference data service hands approved rows to P1 through DataProductAccessLoader'; Template and Rules v1 R3 'Parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043) P3 rwb-case'; DP-07
proposed: The approved load arrives as reference data for table code data_product_access through the rwb-case reference-data contract, with a handler implemented in rwb-source-data; the service exposes no load endpoint of its own and the DataProductAccessLoader interface becomes that handler.

title: The DB slice of this legacy key cannot deliver the table DDL, because two other stories already create the tables
source: RWB-P1-E1001-APP sections 1, 4 and 12.7 (data_product, data_product_access, sys_objects, sys_fields and sys_field_version in rwb_source_data); RWB-P1-E1069-DB section 12.7 (the four extension tables); WP B-P1-01 story line RWB-P1-E1016-DB; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29
section: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria AC7; 12 Contract 12.7; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: RWB-P1-E1001-APP creates the five metadata and access tables in schema rwb_source_data and RWB-P1-E1069-DB creates the four extension tables, so the DB story of this legacy key cannot deliver the DDL the legacy story names. The Work Package gives the DB story no explicit deliverable list, so the boundary of its slice is ambiguous and a second copy of a table would be a duplicate object on the same sequence.
evidence: RWB-P1-E1001-APP 'creates P1's 13 tables in rwb_source_data ... and the catalog table data_product'; RWB-P1-E1069-DB 'the four extension tables ... in schema rwb_source_data'; WP B-P1-01 gives RWB-P1-E1016-DB no acs and no other object list
proposed: E1016-DB delivers the three indexes, the read model v_data_product_catalog, the DPA-2026.11 seed, the 122/1,366 dictionary conformance check and the schema checks; it creates no table that RWB-P1-E1001-APP or RWB-P1-E1069-DB already creates, owns no masking row, and a repeated run changes nothing.

title: The case list extract file, the outbound file adapter and the 07:30 Power BI data set have no target after the data lake is removed
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-002 section 4 steps 9 and 10, section 7 AC2 and AC9, section 12 job step output, section 13 and section 19; TSD P1 v3 T5.1 row INT-19 'Data lake and Power BI'; Arch v5 slides 2, 7, 37 and 42 (INT-19 and INT-20 removed); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-17
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.2; 12.9; 13; 17; 19
description: The legacy story ends by writing a CSV extract for the business date and handing it to the outbound file adapter, and it checks PUBLISHED when that hand-off fails; a Power BI data set on the lake file refreshes at 07:30. Arch v5 removes the data lake and INT-19 and INT-20, so the target has no extract file, no adapter and no data set, and two legacy criteria name artefacts that no longer exist: AC2 asserts the filters of the 'Case list v1' data set and AC9 asserts a failed transfer. No source document says who reads the released rows instead, or how the release stays visible once the file is gone.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-002 section 4 step 9 'sends the extract file for the business date to the data lake through the outbound file adapter only when the publish status is RELEASED' and step 10 'Power BI: refreshes the data set at 07:30'; section 7 AC9 'Given the outbound file adapter fails all its retries for the 2026-11-30 extract file'; TSD P1 v3 T5.1 row INT-19 'Data lake and Power BI, Out, Case list publish (case_list_row)'; Arch v5 slide 37 'Data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20) - Removed: reports from rwb-reporting'; slide 7 'Data lake / Power BI not connected'
proposed: Read the released rows by contract instead of by file: GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate} answers the publish_status and the row count, GET /case-list/rows answers the paged rows in the 19-column order, and the snapshot(page) activity serves an in-namespace caller. rwb-case reads them for SCR-02 and rwb-reporting for its measures. The publish_status gate of RWB-P1-E1011-APP is kept as the release point. AC2 is read as the columns, the filters and the refresh line of those answers; AC9 is kept as history with no lake target, and the PUBLISHED check answers YES when a date is RELEASED and NO when it is HELD.

title: The case-list read operations and their answer shapes are not specified in Arch v5 or in TSD P1
source: Arch v5 slides 15 and 41 (P1 first API path /customers/{id}; the case list is not among the P1 operations); TSD P1 v3 appendix T-A.1 (API-P1-001, 002, 003 and 009 only, no case-list operation); FSD P1 v3 A2.18 (the case list is a Power BI report, not an operation); Template and Rules v1 section R7.2 s12
description: The target reading of the legacy story needs the released case list to be readable by rwb-case for the SCR-02 screen and by rwb-reporting for its measures, but no source gives the operations that serve it. TSD P1 v3 lists four P1 operations and none is a case-list read; Arch v5 slide 15 names snapshot(page) as an activity without an input or output shape; the ownership ruling gives the case list API and screen to rwb-case while the row table stays with P1, which leaves the read path between the two services undefined. The legacy story only had a file, so no operation, path, page shape or column order exists to copy.
evidence: TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 rows API-P1-001 GET /admin/jobs, API-P1-002 POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun, API-P1-003 GET /admin/reconciliation/results, API-P1-009 GET /data-products/freshness and no other; Arch v5 slide 15 'TMP Act: listEligibleAccounts, snapshot(page)'; plan ownership ruling ASM-A6-tables-2 'the case list API and screen stay P3'
proposed: Fixed in RWB-P1-E1002-CON and RWB-P1-E1002-APP: GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate} answers businessDate, publishStatus, rowCount and refreshedAt; GET /case-list/rows answers the paged rows in the 19-column order DF-RPT-001 to DF-RPT-019 filtered by businessDate, team, queue and product; the snapshot(page) activity takes the business date and the page and returns the same rows. A PENDING or HELD date answers its status and no rows. The maximum page size and the sort key stay open with the contract review.

title: The case-list workflow name, the schedule name and the 07:15 fallback are not specified
source: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-04 row (owner rwb-source-data, mechanism event-triggered workflow); Arch v5 slide 15 (Workflow: AceIngestCheck, reconciliation; Act: listEligibleAccounts, snapshot(page)); TSD P1 v3 T4 and T5.3 (no workflow or schedule name); Legacy RWB-E1-002 section 3 and section 7 AC6 (the 07:15 wait)
description: Arch v5 says JOB-04 becomes an event-triggered workflow in rwb-source-data and names only the activities listEligibleAccounts and snapshot(page); it names no workflow and no schedule for the case list build, and TSD P1 v3 keeps no Temporal section naming one. The legacy story starts the step when JOB-03 completes and, if it has not, at 07:15 by the parameter caselist.allocation.wait.until. Without a fixed workflow name, schedule name and fallback time, the build, contract, operations and integration stories of this key would each register a different name for the same daily build.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 'JOB-04 | Reconciliation | Airflow: ACE data ready | rwb-source-data | event-triggered workflow'; slide 15 'TMP Act: listEligibleAccounts, snapshot(page) ? Workflow: AceIngestCheck, reconciliation'; legacy RWB-E1-002 section 3 'caselist.allocation.wait.until 07:15' and section 7 AC6 'When the case list step starts at 07:15'
proposed: Fixed in RWB-P1-E1002-APP, RWB-P1-E1002-CON and RWB-P1-E1002-OPS: CaseListBuildWorkflow, one run per business date with workflow ID = business date, started by rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 and by the DailyCaseList Schedule at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and a one-business-date catch-up window; the 07:15 value is the legacy wait kept unchanged and is read from caselist.allocation.wait.until.

title: retention_rule ownership: TSD P1 v3 keeps it in P1, the Ownership Map and Arch v5 move retention to P5
source: RWB-E1-017; TSD P1 v3 T3.6; Ownership Map rulings for retention_rule and retention_action (ASM-A6-tables-10); Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44 (JOB-17 in rwb-document)
description: The legacy story holds retention_rule in the recovery schema and runs JOB-17 from a Quartz trigger in the same module, and TSD P1 v3 T3.6 still defines retention_rule as a table P1 owns. The Ownership Map rules retention_rule and retention_action to P5 rwb-document and Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44 put the retention Schedule JOB-17 in rwb-document, so rwb-source-data would hold a rule table and a Schedule that another service owns.
evidence: TSD P1 v3 T3.6 defines retention_rule with DF-REF-116 to DF-REF-126 as a Workbench table of P1; Ownership Map table rulings for retention_rule and retention_action give P5 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-10; Architecture v5 slide 16 (P5 IN: Schedule: retention), slide 41 (P5 owns retention) and slide 44 (JOB-17 Retention, monthly 1st Sunday, owner rwb-document, mechanism Schedule).
proposed: Apply the Ownership Map: P5 rwb-document owns retention_rule, retention_action, the load and the JOB-17 Schedule; P1 holds no rule table and no Schedule, receives the rule version, the run date and the rules in the run request, validates them against its own tables and applies them to its own eight tables.

title: The rwb-source-data retention-run contract shape is not specified
source: RWB-E1-017 sections 4, 5 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 15 and 44; Ownership Map API list for P1
description: The legacy story starts the retention inside the module and exposes no operation for it, and neither Arch v5 nor the API Specification names an operation by which another service starts a retention run on rwb-source-data or reads the run record. The request fields, the answer fields, the 202 with a run id, the 409 of an active run and the response field names are therefore absent from every source.
evidence: RWB-E1-017 sections 4, 5 and 12 (Quartz trigger, GET /admin/jobs and POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun only); Architecture v5 slide 15 (P1 IN and OUT lines, no retention operation); Ownership Map API list for P1 (admin jobs, data products, dictionary, contracts, freshness); TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1 endpoint inventory.
proposed: Fix POST /retention-runs and GET /retention-runs/{runId} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1, with the rule version, the run date and the rules in the request and status, counts per table, rule version, archive location and held cases in the answer; the field-level detail is settled in RWB-P1-E1017-CON.

title: The write-once archive contract (container, path and manifest) belongs to RWB-PLT-TE012-APP and is not specified
source: RWB-E1-017 preconditions, AC1 and section 12; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29; RWB-PLT-TE012-APP
description: The legacy story names the write-once archive container, the path retention/YYYY-MM-DD/<table>/ and a manifest of the row count and the SHA-256 per file, but the container contract itself (its account, credential scope, immutability policy, request shape and manifest schema) is owned by RWB-PLT-TE012-APP and appears in none of the source documents read for this story.
evidence: RWB-E1-017 preconditions (write-once archive container in each environment, writable by SY-DATALOAD), AC1 (retention/2026-12-06/interaction/), section 12 (manifest, row count and SHA-256 per file); Architecture v5 slide 11 (File call type: manifest fileId, batchId, sha256, record count); slide 29 (Blob storage with WORM, rwb-document only); RWB-PLT-TE012-APP is listed as an external dependency of this story.
proposed: Keep the legacy path retention/YYYY-MM-DD/<table>/ and the manifest as a row count and a SHA-256 per file, written under the service's own credential and read back before any delete; the container's own contract and immutability policy stay with RWB-PLT-TE012-APP.

title: The legal-hold query is a published interface with no REST path in the sources
source: RWB-E1-017 section 12 (CaseHoldQuery); Architecture v5 slides 11, 14 and 41; Ownership Map (case is P3)
description: The legacy story publishes CaseHoldQuery with casesOnLegalHold() and caseNumbers(...) as an in-process Java interface of the case module. In the target rwb-case is another service, so the answer is a contract call, but no source names a REST path, a request or a response shape for it, and the Ownership Map lists no case legal-hold operation.
evidence: RWB-E1-017 section 12 (Published interfaces: CaseHoldQuery with casesOnLegalHold and caseNumbers); Architecture v5 slide 11 (REST contract, one hop, 2 s; Temporal typed interface); slide 14 (P3 owns the case); slide 41 (P3 owns case and CMMN state); Ownership Map API list for P3.
proposed: Consume the published CaseHoldQuery interface of rwb-case with casesOnLegalHold and caseNumbers, one hop with a 2 s budget, through its contract fake on Day 1; no case table is read by SQL and the transport detail is settled with rwb-case in RWB-P1-E1017-CON.

title: Freshness stamp: the source time and the load time of data_product_load are mapped differently by TSD P1 T3.6 and by FSD P1 A2.14 with legacy AC1
source: Technical Specifications P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.6 (data_product_load field table) and T3.7; Functional Specifications P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14.2 (field table) and its open point OQ-P1-04; legacy RWB-E1-015 AC1, section 4 step 2 and section 11 DF-OPS-005 and DF-OPS-006
description: One combined conflict row for the two time columns of the freshness stamp. (1) source_extracted_at: TSD P1 v3 T3.6 sources it from v_ace_batch_status.completed_at, while FSD P1 v3 A2.14.2 sources it from started_at and cites the open point OQ-P1-04, and the legacy story writes it from started_at. (2) loaded_at: TSD P1 v3 T3.6 describes it as the moment the stamp was written, while FSD P1 v3 A2.14.2 and the legacy story take it from completed_at. R-PREC ranks the TSD above the FSD, so the ruling cannot be read off the precedence list alone; the reading that keeps every legacy acceptance value is taken and the conflict is recorded.
evidence: TSD P1 v3 T3.6 data_product_load row DF-OPS-005 reads 'Workbench, from v_ace_batch_status.completed_at' and row DF-OPS-006 reads 'Workbench; when the stamp was written'; FSD P1 v3 A2.14.2 reads source_extracted_at 'started_at (OQ-P1-04)' and loaded_at 'completed_at'; legacy RWB-E1-015 section 4 step 2 writes source_extracted_at from started_at and loaded_at from completed_at, and AC1 asserts source time 2026-11-30T23:30+07:00 with load time 2026-12-01T05:40+07:00 for a batch row started 23:30 and completed 05:40.
area: Data (P1) freshness stamp: source and load time mapping
proposed: Keep the FSD A2.14 reading and the legacy values: source_extracted_at from started_at and loaded_at from completed_at, and correct TSD P1 T3.6 in its next version.

title: AceDataReady and AceDataLate: the payload fields are fixed but the CloudEvents envelope attributes, the event key, the registry subject and the login on the security scheme are fixed by no source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 15 and 43 (rows 26 and 27); TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T5.3; legacy RWB-E1-015 section 12; Template and Rules v1 ?R5.5 DP-09, DP-14 and DP-02
section: ?12.1 REST operations provided, ?12.3 Events published, ?12.5 Workflows and activities, ?10 Authority
description: One combined missing-value row. (1) The envelope: slide 11 fixes CloudEvents 1.0 in Kafka binary mode with a JSON Schema registry, but no source names which envelope attributes this tuple carries or what the subject is. (2) The payload is given as seven fields by TSD P1 T5.3 with no type, no nullability and no field-level schema. (3) The event key: the case events are keyed by caseId, and a freshness event has no case, so no source fixes its key. (4) The registry subject of rwb.source-data.events.v1 and its compatibility level are platform values. (5) The per-service login name behind the contract security scheme is named by no source.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 43 lists AceDataReady and AceDataLate with producer rwb-source-data and their consumers and slide 11 fixes 'CloudEvents 1.0, binary mode' and 'JSON Schema registry, backward compatible', with no attribute list for this topic; TSD P1 v3 T5.3 states 'Payload for both: eventId, occurredAt, schemaVersion, sourceSystem, businessDate, status, completedAt' and nothing more; the legacy story names the two events and gives no envelope; no source names the login of this service.
area: Integration (P1) freshness events and contract identity
proposed: Fix the envelope attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype with subject set to the source system, key the events by sourceSystem and businessDate, keep the seven payload fields with their types fixed in the AsyncAPI document, and have the platform event owner name the registry subject; reference the login as 'the rwb_source_data login (DP-02)' until it is allocated.

title: Cut-off Schedules: the Schedule names, the per-product expected_by values beyond 08:00 and MON 08:00, the catch-up window and the deployment capacity are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 44; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.7; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14.2; legacy RWB-E1-015 section 3 and section 12
section: ?12.6 Schedules, ?11 Data, ?15 Screens and states, and the operations story ?11 Data and ?13 capacity
description: One combined missing-value row for the cut-off and deployment values of this key. (1) No source names a cut-off Schedule or gives a naming rule for one; the story therefore fixes one Schedule per source-fed data product, named from the product code. (2) The expected-by values are known only for the two rows the legacy Background seeds, 08:00 for the daily products and MON 08:00 for the weekly DP06; the values for the remaining products are catalog data no source lists. (3) The overlap policy is fixed as SKIP by slide 44 and the catch-up window is named but not sized. (4) The deployment capacity, the KEDA thresholds, the replica counts and the probe timings are environment values no source states, and so are the reflow route and the panel field list the operations and app stories must reference.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives 'a Temporal Schedule (cron, with overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window)' for the jobs of the owning service and no Schedule name; TSD P1 v3 T3.7 reads 'The source cut-off (configuration, per source)' without values; FSD P1 v3 A2.14.2 gives the field 'expected_by' with no value list; the legacy story seeds 08:00 and MON 08:00 and states that the values are data rows owned by the data steward (DL11, BR7).
proposed: Keep data_product.expected_by as the only source of a cut-off, register one Schedule per source-fed product from the data row, and carry the name pattern, the catch-up window and the capacity numbers as values of the operations story; extend the catalog with the remaining products' expected-by values once the data steward confirms them.

title: The two lake extracts and the Power BI data set have no successor in the target, while the legacy story still writes them and reads the report
source: Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 4, 5, 12, 13 and 15 and AC1, AC2, AC5; FSD P1 v3 A2.12 (data lake extract, Power BI report, 07:30 refresh) and AC-EXC-P1-012-02; TSD P1 v3 T5.1 (INT-19 Data lake and Power BI); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2 ('ACE database; no data lake connection'), 37 ('no data lake') and 44; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-17
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.1; 12.9; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story ends in two CSV extracts in the data lake, reconciliation/<businessDate>.csv and data-quality/<businessDate>.csv, written through the outbound adapter INT-19, and a Power BI report 'Reconciliation and data quality' that refreshes from them at 07:30. Architecture v5 removes the data lake connection and DP-17 retires INT-19 and INT-20, so neither extract has a target. No source states what replaces them, where the reader gets the variance and the break rows, or what happens to the 07:30 refresh. Read literally, the slice would have to build a file path that the architecture forbids; read as a removal, the story has no stated read path.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 12 'Output ... extracts reconciliation/<businessDate>.csv and data-quality/<businessDate>.csv to the data lake through the outbound adapter (INT-19)' and AC5 'the case list extract is sent to the lake'; FSD P1 v3 A2.12.2 'Writes the extract to the data lake' and AC-EXC-P1-012-02 'the data lake load area does not answer'; TSD P1 v3 T5.1 row INT-19 'Data lake and Power BI, Out, Workbench, Daily'; Architecture v5 slide 2 'ACE database; no data lake connection' and slide 37 'no data lake'; Template and Rules DP-17 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting'
proposed: Read the two extracts and the Power BI data set as removed. The results are exposed by GET /admin/reconciliation/results and GET /admin/reconciliation/results/{resultId} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1 (API-P1-003), and rwb-reporting reads them through that contract for its dashboards, so no lake target, no file and no report refresh exists in any story of this key. Keep the legacy sentences that name the lake as history in the legacy story and in the gap register, and read the AC5 clause 'the case list extract is sent to the lake' as the release of the case list for the read path of RWB-P1-E1002-APP.

title: TSD P1 keeps REC-03, REC-04 and a cross-estate REC-05 inside P1 while the Change Register gives rwb-case, rwb-asset and rwb-comms their own slices of the same legacy key
source: Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 2, 4, 8, 11 and 16 (REC-01 to REC-05, treatment, proceeds, listing, asset_sale, debt_sale_account, notice, document); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 ('REC-01 and REC-02 write reconciliation_result rows. A REC-05 orphan raises a break') and T-A.2 API-P1-003; FSD P1 v3 A2.11 and A2.12 (REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05 only); Recovery Workbench Microservice Change Register v1 row RWB-E1-011 (slices RWB-P1-E1011-APP, RWB-P3-E1011-APP, RWB-S5-E1011-APP, RWB-P6-E1011-APP, RWB-P1-E1011-OPS, RWB-ITG-E1011-ITG, RWB-P1-E1011-CON); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (treatment S2, proceeds P8)
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 12.2; 16 Test cases; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story runs five checks in one step: REC-01 count, REC-02 balance, REC-03 approved treatments not booked, REC-04 payments unmatched to proceeds, and REC-05 over every business key on every Workbench table. The Change Register splits the key across rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-asset and rwb-comms, and the Ownership Map gives treatment to S2 and proceeds to P8, so REC-03, REC-04 and the REC-05 keys of the other services' tables cannot be P1's. TSD P1 v3 still describes the three checks in the P1 module and gives REC-05 over case_account, case_party and the extension keys, and FSD P1 v3 A2.11 already narrows the module to REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05. No source states which rows P1 writes after the split, so the count of fifteen rows in legacy AC5 and AC6 and the six rows of FSD A2.12 disagree.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 4 steps 5, 6 and 7 ('REC-03 counts approved restructure treatments', 'REC-04 matches v_ace_payment rows ... to proceeds', 'REC-05 resolves every account_key, person_key, asset_key, payment_code and contact_key on a Workbench table') and AC5 'the system replaces the fifteen results'; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 table 'REC-01 | ... | REC-02 | ... | REC-05 | Every business key on a Workbench row resolves in its view (case_account.account_key, case_party.person_key, the extension keys)'; FSD P1 v3 AC-P1-011-01 'six reconciliation_result rows are written, REC-01 and REC-02 for each product'; Change Register row RWB-E1-011 with the four service slices; ownership.json treatment owner S2 and proceeds owner P8
proposed: Keep REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05 over P1's own tables in RWB-P1-E1011-APP, which means the REC-01 and REC-02 rows per product group plus the REC-05 orphan list and no REC-03 or REC-04 row. Leave REC-03 to RWB-P3-E1011-APP and RWB-S5-E1011-APP, REC-04 to RWB-P6-E1011-APP and the payment slice, and the REC-05 keys of rwb-case, rwb-asset and rwb-comms to those same slices, with the whole journey proven in RWB-ITG-E1011-ITG. Keep the legacy twelve table names in section 11 as history and read the fifteen-row sentences of AC5 and AC6 as the legacy count of five checks over three product groups.
